# requireNonRegExp

<link-summary>Returns the value after checking that it is not a regular expression.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireNonRegExp() — Returns the value after checking that it is not a regular expression. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireNonRegExp<T>(
  value: T | RegExp,
  message: string = "Expected a value that is not a regular expression."
): T;
```

Identified by its internal tag rather than by `instanceof`, so a regular expression from another frame is recognised too.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                                                       | Type          | Description                                                   |
| :------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | :------------ | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                                                                         | `T \| RegExp` | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected a value that is not a regular expression."` | `string`      | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`T` — the same value, with a regular expression excluded from its type.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition                          |
| :------------------------- | :--------------------------------- |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is a regular expression. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireNonRegExp("/a/"); // => "/a/"
requireNonRegExp({}); // => {}
requireNonRegExp(/a/); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireNonRegExp(new RegExp("a")); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
